newsitem.title: GERMANY: Commerzbank to integrate derivatives unit.
newsitem.headline: Commerzbank to integrate derivatives unit.

text.p: Germany's Commerzbank AG said on Tuesday it would integrate Commerz Financial Products GmbH (CFP) into the main bank as of January 1 1998, marking the end of the derivatives unit's start-up phase.
The unit's three operating areas -- stocks, interest rates and foreign exchange derivatives -- would be directly linked with the underlying business divisions, Commerzbank said in a statement.
The bank said that matching underlying business with derivatives business should result in a strong synergy effect and strengthen its investment banking division, which continued to expand.
CFP started operations in 1996 and posted an operating profit of 131 million marks in 1996 and 93 million marks for the first six months of 1997. The unit now has 250 staff.
Commerzbank also said it would set up a product development unit in 1998. In addition, it would place all Treasury and foreign exchange activities under the investment banking corporate division.
